Subject: Post-demo: Integration fit & SDK / function-calling notes

Hi Benjamin / Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we can align the technical deep dive with your procurement timeline.

High-level pain & goals (as we heard them)
- Latency-sensitive in-product assistant (sub-150ms per turn target for live chat UX)
- Relevance + precision for search across structured logs (embeddings + reranking)
- Predictable unit costs for heavy query volume (50k–200k queries/day) and ability to cap spend per environment
- Data residency + auditability for regulated customers (on-prem or VPC option)

Integration & product-fit notes from the demo
- SDK & API: You liked the simple SDK flow; Rishi noted our SDK will need a small wrapper to surface your existing request/response envelope. We can provide a thin adapter example in JS and Python in the next 48 hours.
- Function calling: You want structured outputs to surface discrete actions (create-ticket, load-record). Redwood’s function-calling schema maps to those actions; we’ll share a sample schema for your ticketing workflow.
- Streaming: For the live assistant, streaming partial tokens for UI responsiveness is required. We recommend streaming + prefix caching to meet your latency SLOs.
- Embeddings & reranking: Best path is embeddings for candidate recall and a lightweight reranker (model variant with conservative decoding) for precision. We’ll propose a batching and caching profile to keep cost predictable.

Open questions you flagged
1) On-prem / VPC support: what exact network egress/inbound rules your security team expects and whether HSM/KMS is required.
2) Footprint: GPU sizing for your expected concurrency (50–150 concurrent chat sessions during peak).
3) Procurement: target date for purchase order and whether you need a SOC-2 package before contracting.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (integration checklist), rough-sow-acme-20260302.pdf (high-level SOW draft)

Next steps (proposed)
- Benjamin / Sarah: confirm top 3 success metrics and whether on-prem is required by EOD Wed (2026-03-04).
- Redwood: we (Rishi + Priyom) to produce a tech deep-dive agenda and lightweight adapter examples (JS + Python) by Wed EOD.
- Schedule a 60-min technical session next week with your infra/security and our solutions engineers — proposed slots attached in calendar invite.

If you’d prefer we triage the streaming + function-calling flow first, we can make that the focus for the technical session.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers and clarifications from our side:

- Success metrics: (1) median assistant response latency < 150ms at 95th pct, (2) +15% precision on top-3 search results after reranking, (3) reduce manual triage volume by 30% in first 90 days.
- On-prem vs VPC: We prefer a VPC-hosted control plane but need the model runtime to be able to run in our AWS VPC (private subnet) or on a co-lo in our region — this is negotiable but data cannot leave country boundaries.
- Security: We need SOC 2 evidence and a short network requirements doc for our infra team.
- Function calling: yes — structured outputs are critical. We’ll need to map Redwood function schemas to our ticketing API.
- Streaming: required for the agent UI. If streaming imposes latency variability, we’d like an option to degrade gracefully (e.g., switch to a lower-cost batch path on spikes).

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to have vendor selection by end of Q2 and expect a PO in June. That said, we may run a pilot earlier if the tech fit looks good.

I’ve asked Sarah to include our security lead on the tech session invite. Two asks for Redwood before the deep dive:
1) brief note on data residency options and whether any PII will be logged by default;
2) a ballpark GPU sizing estimate for 100 concurrent sessions (so our infra team has a starting point).

Thanks —
Ben
VP Product, Acme Analytics
benjamin.ward@acmeanalytics.com
